# Releasing

Stable releases are cut by pushing an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag. The `Release` workflow (`.github/workflows/github-release.yml`) does everything else: it builds the VSIX, creates the GitHub release with generated notes, checks that the tests passed, publishes to the Visual Studio Marketplace, records the version on `main` and finally marks the release as latest.

## Stable releases

1. Pick a PR merge commit on `main` whose `Run tests` run is green.

   ```
   git fetch origin
   git log --merges --first-parent --oneline origin/main
   gh run list --workflow test.yml --commit <sha>
   ```

2. Tag that commit and push the tag.

   ```
   git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Release vX.Y.Z" <sha>
   git push origin vX.Y.Z
   ```

`X.Y.Z` must exceed the highest published stable release, and the tagged commit must descend from it. No version, changelog or release notes edits are made beforehand: the workflow writes the version into the build, the notes are generated from merged PRs, and the version is recorded on `main` afterwards.

## Tagging rule

- The tag is annotated and points at the PR merge commit on `main`. Never tag the `chore(release): set version to ...` bot commit. It has no `Run tests` run, because pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` start no workflow, so the test gate would fail.
- When the bot commit is the tip of `main`, tag the merge commit below it.
- The test gate accepts any green `test.yml` run for the tagged commit, so a green `pull_request` run for a PR-head commit also passes it. That run tested the merge with the base of its time, not the commit itself. Tagging the merge commit avoids relying on that: its `push` run on `main` tested exactly the released tree.

## What the workflow does

Stable tags run all eight jobs, in this order:

| # | Job name | Job id | What it does |
|---|----------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | Resolve Release Metadata | `metadata` | Classifies the tag, validates it (shape, version ordering, ancestry, dispatch rules) and resolves the commit, version and notes range |
| 2 | Build VSIX | `build` | Checks out the tag, injects the version, builds the solution and verifies the version inside the VSIX |
| 3 | Create Release | `create-release` | Creates or updates the GitHub release with generated notes. The release is created as not latest |
| 4 | Upload Release Assets | `upload` | Attaches the VSIX to the release; assets already attached are skipped |
| 5 | Verify Tests Passed | `test-gate` | Requires a successful `Run tests` run for the tagged commit |
| 6 | Publish to Visual Studio Marketplace | `publish` | Publishes the VSIX attached to the release (runs in the `marketplace` environment) |
| 7 | Record Released Version | `record-version` | Bot commit to `main` that sets the released version in the manifest and the version constant |
| 8 | Mark Release Latest | `promote` | Marks the release as latest, only if no newer release is already latest |

The release is created not latest and promoted last, so "latest" never points at a version that failed to publish.

Runs are serialised by the `github-release` concurrency group. Queued runs are kept rather than cancelled, so two tags pushed close together are processed one after the other.

Test tags (`vX.Y.Z-test.<sha>`) run only `metadata`, `build`, `create-release` and `upload`. They never reach the gate, publish, record or promote stages.

## Release notes

Notes are generated by GitHub from `.github/release.yml`. PRs are grouped by label:

| Section | Labels |
|---------|--------|
| Breaking Changes | `breaking-change`, `breaking` |
| Features | `feature`, `enhancement` |
| Bug Fixes | `bug`, `fix`, `defect` |
| Security | `security` |
| Documentation | `documentation`, `docs` |
| Dependencies | `dependencies` |
| Other Changes | everything else |

Excluded from the notes: PRs labelled `ignore-for-release` or `skip-changelog`, and PRs authored by `dependabot` or `github-actions`.

Labels are not enforced. An unlabelled PR lands in Other Changes. The repository currently has the labels `bug`, `documentation` and `enhancement`; the others (`breaking-change`, `breaking`, `feature`, `fix`, `defect`, `security`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `ignore-for-release`, `skip-changelog`) can be created when needed.

## Recovery

Any stage can fail after earlier stages have had their effect. Complete the release by dispatching the workflow for the existing tag:

```
gh workflow run github-release.yml --ref main -f tag=vX.Y.Z
```

- The dispatch must come from `main` (`--ref main`) and the tag must already exist.
- The stages re-run with these skip rules:

  | Stage | Re-run behaviour |
  |-------|------------------|
  | `metadata` | Recomputed; fails if the tag does not exist |
  | `build` | Always rebuilt |
  | `create-release` | The existing release is updated, never duplicated |
  | `upload` | Only assets missing on the release are attached |
  | `test-gate` | Re-evaluated against the current runs |
  | `publish` | Skipped when the version is already on the Marketplace |
  | `record-version` | Skipped when `main` is already at or above the version |
  | `promote` | Unchanged when already latest; left alone when a newer release is latest |

- Recovering an older tag never lowers the version on `main` and never moves latest away from a newer release.
- A gate failure because tests are still running is cleared by dispatching again after they finish. A gate failure because tests failed needs a fix on `main` and a new tag, or a re-run of the failed tests.
- Recovery regenerates the notes and overwrites a hand-edited release body.
- The workflow definition and the release helper (`.github/release-flow.ps1` and `.github/release-flow.psm1`) both come from `main`, while the sources, README and publish manifest come from the tag. A helper fix merged to `main` is therefore used by the next recovery dispatch, and tags that predate the helper can be recovered.

## Dry run

```
gh workflow run github-release.yml --ref main -f tag=v0.9.1 -f dry_run=true
```

A dry run uses an existing stable tag. It runs `metadata` plus the Azure and publisher logins of the `publish` job only, in the `marketplace` environment. It creates no release, builds nothing, publishes nothing, commits nothing and promotes nothing. It is used to prove the Azure credential and the publish rights. Test tags are rejected.

## Test releases

Test releases are prereleases for trying a build, with no Marketplace publish.

```
make tag-test-release BUMP=minor
pwsh -File tag-test-release.ps1 -Bump patch -WhatIf
pwsh -File tag-test-release.ps1 -Bump patch -NoPush
```

- `BUMP` is `patch`, `minor` or `major`, and defaults to `patch`.
- `-WhatIf` prints the tag that would be created. `-NoPush` creates the tag locally without pushing it.
- Prerequisites: `gh` installed and authenticated (`gh auth login`), and a clean worktree.
- NEXT comes from the highest published stable release, bumped by `BUMP`. The tag is `vNEXT-test.<sha>` on the current `HEAD`.
- The workflow checks the tag shape, the sha prefix and that the base version exceeds the previous stable release.
- The result is a prerelease with the VSIX and the test banner. There is no Marketplace publish, no write to `main` and no change to latest.

### Installing a test release

Download `Codescene.VSExtension.VS2022.vsix` from the prerelease and install it by double-clicking it (the VSIX installer). The version shown is the base `X.Y.Z`, so repeated test builds of the same base may not count as upgrades; uninstall the previous test build first when the installer reports it as already installed.

## Changelog history

Release notes before this flow lived in `CHANGELOG.md`. The migration script copies those sections into the bodies of the matching GitHub releases.

```
pwsh -File .github/migrate-changelog-to-releases.ps1
pwsh -File .github/migrate-changelog-to-releases.ps1 --apply
```

- Without `--apply` it is a dry run that reports what it would change.
- `--file <path>` overrides the source.
- The source is the last committed `CHANGELOG.md` in Git history (the file is removed from the working tree).
- Only published stable releases are touched, and releases are never created. Sections with no matching release are reported.
- The script is safe to re-run: the migrated text sits in a delimited block that is replaced, not appended again.

## Environment facts

- The `publish` job runs in the `marketplace` environment. GitHub creates the environment on the first run that names it. It has no required reviewers.
- The Azure federated credential used for publishing must accept the subject `repo:codescene-oss/codescene-vs:environment:marketplace`. The credential is developer-owned.
- An optional deployment policy can limit the `marketplace` environment to `main` and `v*` tags.
- The `record-version` job pushes to `main` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. This works because `main` has no branch protection or rulesets. Adding either would break the version record.
